meaning: to work or study late into the night
literal_translation: trabalhar ou estudar até tarde da noite
example: She had to burn the midnight oil to finish the report before the deadline.
origin: Comes from the time when people used oil lamps to light their work late at night

wrong_meanings.meaning: to waste money on expensive fuel
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with spending money. It describes working or studying late.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to get up very early in the morning
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which refers to working at night, not at dawn.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to stop working because you are tired
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes staying up and working late, not giving up or resting.

explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' comes from the time when oil lamps lit people's work after dark. It means working or studying late into the night, usually because there is a lot to do or a deadline to meet.
